title: One of Each Pair, by Coin Toss

scenes.visual: THE WORLD, kept for both chapters (16:9, dark navy background). Chromosomes are drawn as rounded rods with a narrow waist, the centromere, shown as a white dot. COLOURS, same in every scene: first pair BLUE and ORANGE; second pair GREEN and PURPLE. Allele labels appear on screen only, in white: 'A' on the blue rod, 'a' on the orange rod, 'B' on the green rod, 'b' on the purple rod. A CENTROMERE COUNTER sits in the top-right corner of every frame where cells are counted: a small white box reading 'centromeres: N' for each cell shown. Numbers always appear on screen as text. Title card 'One of Each Pair, by Coin Toss' fades in, centred, over a faint blue and orange rod pair drifting behind it.

scenes.tts: Which four chromosomes does a fruit fly sperm get? The fly's body cells hold eight. Its eggs and sperm hold four, one from each of four pairs.
scenes.visual: Title fades. A round fly cell holds eight rods in four colour-matched pairs (blue/orange and three grey pairs). Counter: 'centromeres: 8'. The cell narrows into a sperm shape holding four rods, one of each pair; counter changes to 'centromeres: 4'. A white question mark hovers over the four rods.
scenes.narration: Which four chromosomes does a fruit fly sperm get? The fly's body cells hold eight. Its eggs and sperm hold four, one from each of four pairs.

scenes.tts: Mendel worked out his laws from counts of peas. He never saw what did the separating.
scenes.visual: Left: a small pea pod with a tally of seeds and the label 'Mendel: counts'. Right: the fly cell, blurred, with a 'closed eye' icon over it. The pod slides away and the camera pushes into the fly cell until only the blue and orange rods remain.
scenes.narration: Mendel worked out his laws from counts of peas. He never saw what did the separating.

scenes.tts: These two chromosomes are homologs, one inherited from each parent. They carry the same genes at the same places. But they can carry different versions, called alleles. Blue carries one allele, and orange carries the other. Follow the colours.
scenes.visual: Blue and orange rods side by side, same length. Matching grey bands appear at the same positions on both to mark genes. One band glows on each: label 'A' on the blue rod, 'a' on the orange rod. Labels 'homolog' and 'homolog' under each rod, then a bracket 'one from each parent'. Counter: 'centromeres: 2'.
scenes.narration: These two chromosomes are homologs, one inherited from each parent. They carry the same genes at the same places. But they can carry different versions, called alleles. Blue carries one allele, and orange carries the other. Follow the colours.

scenes.tts: Before meiosis, in S phase, each chromosome is copied. The two copies are sister chromatids, joined at the centromere. Count centromeres, not arms. A copied chromosome is still one chromosome.
scenes.visual: Each rod duplicates into an X-shape of two identical sisters joined at the white centromere dot: blue pair of sisters, orange pair of sisters. Label 'sister chromatids' with arrows. The counter pulses but still reads 'centromeres: 2'; a small note under it: 'chromatids: 4'. The note fades out; the centromere count stays.
scenes.narration: Before meiosis, in S phase, each chromosome is copied. The two copies are sister chromatids, joined at the centromere. Count centromeres, not arms. A copied chromosome is still one chromosome.

scenes.tts: Meiosis is one round of copying, then two divisions. In the first, the homologs find each other and line up side by side. Then the pair sits across the middle of the cell, its homologs facing opposite poles.
scenes.visual: A cell outline appears around the copied blue and orange chromosomes. They slide together and lie side by side along their length. A spindle forms with two white poles, top and bottom; the paired chromosomes move to the cell's equator, blue facing the top pole, orange facing the bottom. Label 'meiosis I'.
scenes.narration: Meiosis is one round of copying, then two divisions. In the first, the homologs find each other and line up side by side. Then the pair sits across the middle of the cell, its homologs facing opposite poles.

scenes.tts: Anaphase one pulls the homologs apart. Each new cell gets one member of the pair. Count its centromeres: one. The cell is already haploid, with one homolog of this pair. That chromosome is still two sister chromatids.
scenes.caption: Anaphase I pulls the homologs apart. Each new cell gets one member of the pair. Count its centromeres: one. The cell is already haploid, with one homolog of this pair. That chromosome is still two sister chromatids.
scenes.visual: Spindle fibres pull blue (still two sisters) to the top and orange (still two sisters) to the bottom. The cell pinches into two. Counter now shows two boxes: 'centromeres: 1' and 'centromeres: 1'. Label 'anaphase I' and 'haploid' on each daughter; each daughter's rod still shows its two sisters.
scenes.narration: Anaphase I pulls the homologs apart. Each new cell gets one member of the pair. Count its centromeres: one. The cell is already haploid, with one homolog of this pair. That chromosome is still two sister chromatids.

scenes.tts: No DNA is copied in between. In the second division, the sisters part. That makes four products. Two carry blue's allele, and two carry orange's.
scenes.visual: Label 'meiosis II'. Each daughter lines its chromosome up; the sisters are pulled apart. Four small round products appear in a row: blue rod 'A', blue rod 'A', orange rod 'a', orange rod 'a'. Counter: four boxes reading 'centromeres: 1'. On-screen tally: '2 A : 2 a'.
scenes.narration: No DNA is copied in between. In the second division, the sisters part. That makes four products. Two carry blue's allele, and two carry orange's.

scenes.tts: That two-and-two split is what Mendel's model expects. It is his law of segregation, seen as chromosome movement.
scenes.visual: The four products stay. A white banner slides across them: 'Segregation = the deal'. A small stack of grey meiosis icons appears behind, each showing the same '2 A : 2 a'. Small grey note: 'expected outcome; rare exceptions in the lesson'.
scenes.narration: That two-and-two split is what Mendel's model expects. It is his law of segregation, seen as chromosome movement.

scenes.tts: Now add a second pair, green and purple, on a different chromosome, carrying a second gene.
scenes.visual: Back to the copied, paired stage in meiosis I. The blue/orange pair sits at the equator; a green/purple pair (copied, sisters joined) slides in beside it. Labels 'B' on green, 'b' on purple. Counter: 'centromeres: 4'.
scenes.narration: Now add a second pair, green and purple, on a different chromosome, carrying a second gene.

scenes.tts: Here is the question. Does the way the blue pair faces the poles change the way the green pair faces?
scenes.visual: Both pairs at the equator. Blue faces the top pole. The green/purple pair glows and wobbles, undecided, with a white question mark beside it. Question card along the bottom: 'Does the blue pair's direction change the green pair's?'
scenes.narration: Here is the question. Does the way the blue pair faces the poles change the way the green pair faces?

scenes.tts: No. Each pair faces the spindle by its own coin toss. Blue may end up with green, or blue with purple.
scenes.visual: Two coins spin, one beside each pair, and land independently. The screen splits into two layouts. Left: blue and green face the top pole; orange and purple face the bottom. Right: blue and purple face the top; orange and green face the bottom. A label under both: 'each pair: its own coin toss'.
scenes.narration: No. Each pair faces the spindle by its own coin toss. Blue may end up with green, or blue with purple.

scenes.tts: Ignoring crossovers for now, one meiosis takes just one of these layouts. So one meiosis gives only two kinds of gamete, two of each.
scenes.visual: The left layout runs both divisions quickly: four products, 'AB', 'AB', 'ab', 'ab'. A box around them reads 'one meiosis: 2 kinds'. A small grey note in the corner: 'no crossovers'.
scenes.narration: Ignoring crossovers for now, one meiosis takes just one of these layouts. So one meiosis gives only two kinds of gamete, two of each.

scenes.tts: Independence shows only when you count many meioses. Both layouts are equally likely. So all four kinds of gamete appear, a quarter each. That is independent assortment.
scenes.visual: Many small meiosis icons run in a grid, each landing on one layout or the other. Four bars rise underneath, labelled 'AB', 'Ab', 'aB', 'ab', in matching colour pairs, settling at equal heights; each bar labelled '1/4'. Banner: 'Independent assortment = the coin tosses, counted over many'.
scenes.narration: Independence shows only when you count many meioses. Both layouts are equally likely. So all four kinds of gamete appear, a quarter each. That is independent assortment.

scenes.tts: Each extra pair is one more coin toss. So the combinations climb fast, with two choices for every pair.
scenes.visual: The fly's four pairs line up at an equator, each with its own spinning coin. On-screen text appears line by line: '4 pairs: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16 combinations', then 'human, 23 pairs: 2^23 ≈ 8.4 million'. A small grey note: 'ignoring crossing over'.
scenes.narration: Each extra pair is one more coin toss. So the combinations climb fast, with two choices for every pair.

scenes.tts: This holds for genes on different chromosomes. Genes close together on one chromosome tend to travel together. And something has to hold each pair together until it is dealt. That is chapter two.
scenes.caption: This holds for genes on different chromosomes. Genes close together on one chromosome tend to travel together. And something has to hold each pair together until it is dealt. That is chapter 2.
scenes.visual: Left panel: two separate pairs with A and B on different chromosomes, labelled 'different chromosomes: independent'. Right panel: one chromosome pair carrying A and B close together, bracketed, labelled 'close together: travel together (linkage)'. Then the camera pushes onto a single blue/orange pair at the equator; a faint dotted outline of something linking them appears, labelled 'chapter 2'.
scenes.narration: This holds for genes on different chromosomes. Genes close together on one chromosome tend to travel together. And something has to hold each pair together until it is dealt. That is chapter 2.

scenes.tts: So here is the idea, in the simple Mendelian model. Meiosis one deals one homolog of each pair to each cell. Each pair is dealt by its own fair coin toss. Meiosis two then splits sisters. Segregation is the deal. Independent assortment is the coin tosses.
scenes.caption: So here is the idea, in the simple Mendelian model. Meiosis I deals one homolog of each pair to each cell. Each pair is dealt by its own fair coin toss. Meiosis II then splits sisters. Segregation is the deal. Independent assortment is the coin tosses.
scenes.visual: Title-card style. Lines appear one at a time, left-aligned, white on navy: 'Meiosis I deals one homolog of each pair.' 'Each pair: its own fair coin toss.' 'Meiosis II splits sisters.' A small grey note in the corner: 'Mendelian model; exceptions in the lesson'. Beneath, two small icons: a dealt pair of cards labelled 'segregation' and a coin labelled 'independent assortment'.
scenes.narration: So here is the idea, in the simple Mendelian model. Meiosis I deals one homolog of each pair to each cell. Each pair is dealt by its own fair coin toss. Meiosis II then splits sisters. Segregation is the deal. Independent assortment is the coin tosses.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed world, large white text, centred: 'Meiosis I deals one homolog per pair, each by coin toss.'
